name: TOE1 (cerebellar abiotrophy)
summary: Cerebellar abiotrophy (CA) of Arabian horses, an inherited loss of the cerebellum's Purkinje cells that leaves the horse unable to coordinate its movements. It is associated with one variant on chromosome 2, TOE1 g.2171G>A, which changes an amino acid in TOE1 (R95H) and also lies in the regulatory region of the neighbouring gene MUTYH, read from the opposite strand; which of the two matters is not settled. It is recessive: carriers are clinically normal, and a horse with two copies is affected, mildly or severely. It occurs almost only in Arabians, where about one horse in five was found to be a carrier, and in breeds with Arabian ancestry. UC Davis writes the genotypes N/N, N/CA and CA/CA. No effect on coat or build is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: TOE1 (cerebellar abiotrophy) carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy. The horse is clinically normal and passes the copy to half its foals. A foal is affected only when both parents pass it on.

phenotypes.name: Cerebellar abiotrophy
phenotypes.description: Two copies. The Purkinje cells of the cerebellum, which coordinate balance and movement, degenerate after birth. The foal may look normal at first; signs usually begin at about six weeks, anywhere from birth to four months. The horse keeps its strength but cannot coordinate it: a head tremor on purposeful movement, staggering, a wide stance, an exaggerated high action of the forelegs, a poor blink response to a threat, easy startling, falls, and in severe cases being unable to rise. Severity runs from a mild head tremor to disabling. There is no cure, and severely affected foals are often put down.

frequencies.population: Arabian, Egypt (5 carriers in 80 horses, none affected; 2021 study)
Bashkir Curly (allele frequency of ca 0.028, Brault and Penedo 2011; brought in by one Arabian stallion; genotype shares worked out from it assuming random mating)
Trakehner (allele frequency of ca 0.0068, Brault and Penedo 2011; carriers at least half-Arabian; genotype shares worked out from it assuming random mating)
Welsh Pony (allele frequency of ca 0.0033, Brault and Penedo 2011; carriers at least half-Arabian; genotype shares worked out from it assuming random mating)
Barb and Arab-Barb (not found; 2021 study, sample size not given)
Arabian (about 20% carriers on average, from screening nearly 11,000 horses; the share of affected horses is not given, and it differs widely between families)
